editor.wizardNoticeTitle: 🎬 Director's Notice: AI drafts the foundation – you direct the film!
editor.wizardNoticeDesc: The Script Wizard generates a narrative draft. For a cohesive movie with seamless flow, review and refine the generated scenes: vary camera perspectives, set match-cuts for continuous action, and harmonize outfits. Unedited AI drafts often feel disconnected in the final video.
editor.btnReadBestPractices: Read Best Practices for Cohesive Scenes
editor.guideModalSubtitle: Practical guide for cinematic AI movies, visual continuity, and director settings
editor.guideSec1Intro: MovieGenerator connects cutting-edge local AI models (ComfyUI Diffusion, Minimax Video, and LM Studio LLMs) into an automated filmmaking pipeline.
editor.guideSec1Phase1Desc: The local LLM analyzes the storyline, harmonizes character wardrobe, and writes detailed Minimax video prompts.
editor.guideSec1Phase2Desc: Generates neutral, high-res reference portraits for each character. Alternatively, upload your own photos with automated AI background removal.
editor.guideSec1Phase3Desc: Generates 3-8 second video shots. Links character portraits and, during match-cuts, the exact final frame of the previous scene.
editor.guideSec1Phase4Desc: Upscales rendered video shots up to 1080p, sharpening textures, edges, and fine details.
editor.guideSec1Phase5Desc: Stitches all shots into a master movie and mixes an optional time-synchronized ACE soundtrack with smart auto-ducking.
editor.guideSec2Title: 🔗 2. Visual Continuity & Scene Cuts (Why Raw Videos Feel Disconnected)
editor.guideSec2Intro: Image-to-Video models render each clip in isolation unless deliberately guided. A cohesive film requires thoughtful cuts, shared locations, and frame references.
editor.guideSec2Rule1Desc: Enable this when physical action continues without a time jump (e.g., Shot 1: Hand grabs door handle; Shot 2: Door swings open from interior). Minimax extracts the final frame of Shot N as the exact starting frame of Shot N+1.
editor.guideSec2Rule1Warning: ⚠️ Important: Only enable Match-Cut at the same location without a time jump! Keep disabled when jumping to a new location.
editor.guideSec2Rule2Desc: Enable 'same_scene' when shifting camera angles or shot sizes within the same room (e.g., cutting from wide shot to close-up). MovieGenerator passes the previous scene as an environmental reference.
editor.guideSec2Rule3Desc: Sequential shots must share identical names in 'Location' (e.g., 'Sunset Beach') and 'Sequence' (e.g., 'Scene 1: The Confession') so the LLM enforces identical lighting and environmental prompts.
editor.guideSec3Intro: The prompt formula for cinematic Minimax shots follows a structured anatomy:
editor.guideSec3Formula: [Camera Framing & Motion] + [<Subject X> (Name) in {Outfit Variables}] + [Physical Action & Gaze] + [Lighting / Atmosphere] + [<d>"Dialogue"</d>]
editor.guideSec3BadLabel: ❌ Vague Prompt (leads to chaotic AI drift):
editor.guideSec3BadExample: "A man and woman stand on the beach and talk about their future and feel very sad."
editor.guideSec3GoodExample: "Medium close-up, camera slowly tracks sideways. <Subject 1> (Elena) in her {elena_top} looks down at the wet sand, tears glistening. <Subject 2> (Noah) steps into frame, placing a gentle hand on her shoulder. Soft golden hour ocean breeze. Elena whispers: <d>\"I don't know if we can make it.\"</d>"
editor.guideSec3RuleSubject: Always use '<Subject X> (Name)': Minimax binds actor reference portraits strictly through these tags! Without tags, random faces appear.
editor.guideSec3RuleDialogue: Spoken words belong inside '<d>...</d>': Words inside these tags are spoken lip-synced. Never place descriptive action inside '<d>'!
editor.guideSec3RuleVariables: Wardrobe Variables & Delta Updates: If clothing changes (e.g. jacket removed), update only that specific variable on the scene. The rest of the wardrobe persists automatically.
editor.guideSec4Title: ⚙️ 4. Director's Control: Turbo LoRA, Steps & Resolution
editor.guideSec4Intro: Director settings let you customize quality, render speed, and visual sharpness per scene:
editor.guideSec4TurboDesc:
• ⚡ Turbo (8 Steps): Up to 2.5x faster! Great for rapid drafting, wide shots, high-speed action, camera dollies, and vehicles.
• 🎯 HQ / No Turbo (20 Steps): Maximum facial stability, subtle expressions, and pristine eyes. Ideal for emotional dialogues and close-ups.
editor.guideSec4ResDesc:
• Default (0.25 MP / 672x384): The proven sweet-spot for Minimax. Fast and VRAM-friendly. Razor-sharp when paired with '2x RealESRGAN'.
• Wide / Native HD (0.45 / 0.75 MP): Ideal for vast landscapes and intricate details when your GPU has ample VRAM.
editor.guideSec5Intro: MovieGenerator scores your completed movie using ComfyUI ACE-Step models without drowning out dialogue or environmental foley.
editor.guideSec5TimingDesc: Clicking 'Suggest Tags with AI' analyzes all scenes and builds a timestamped score progression (e.g. '[00:00-00:07] Intro, gentle acoustic guitar... [00:25-00:35] Climax, outro'). The music mirrors your story arc.
editor.guideSec5DuckingDesc: FFmpeg automatically ducks the music level by 6-8 dB during dialogue and sound effects. When characters pause, the score breathes back up smoothly.
editor.guideSec6Title: 🧙‍♂️ 6. Script Wizard: AI as Co-Writer, You as Director
editor.guideSec6Intro: The Script Wizard is a creative writing partner – but it cannot replace the director's eye for cinematic editing!
editor.guideSec6Step1: 1. Vary shot sizes: Avoid 5 wide shots in a row. Cut between establishing shot, medium shot, and close-up.
editor.guideSec6Step2: 2. Enable Match-Cuts: If physical action spills across two clips, enable Match-Cut on the following shot.
editor.guideSec6Step3: 3. Harmonize script: Click '✨ Harmonize' to align wardrobe variables, props, and Minimax tags across the entire script.
editor.guideSec6Step4: 4. Pace dialogue: For a 6-second shot, limit spoken dialogue in '<d>...</d>' to 1-2 concise sentences.
editor.guideSec6Step5: 5. Fine-tune Director's Control: Set crucial dialogue to HQ (20 Steps) and fast action shots to Turbo (8 Steps).
editor.wizardNoticeShort: AI drafts the foundation – refine camera angles & cuts before rendering.
